subject: ACME MAP: Benchmarking checklist, SLOs & close timeline
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Emma Dawson <emma@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ACME MAP: Benchmarking checklist, SLOs & close timeline

Hi Emma,

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our MAP, we want to fold the performance benchmarking plan and the acceptance criteria into the mutual action plan so we can get to a production decision by the end of July. To make that happen I've sketched a lightweight scope and a proposed close timeline below.

High-level ask: confirm workload definition and SLOs, and agree on run windows so we can schedule dedicated capacity for the run.

Proposed scope (short):
- Workload: 3 canonical prompts + 50 synthetic variations per prompt, mixed short/long contexts (64/512 tokens).
- Targets: median TTFT < 300ms, p95 latency < 650ms, throughput 40 reqs/sec sustained per instance, concurrency up to 80 users for burst tests.
- Success criteria: model variant meets TTFT and p95 thresholds on at least 95% of test samples and output quality delta < 2% against baseline eval set.
- Test types: cold-start TTFT, steady-state throughput, prefix-cached scenarios, and degradation/fallover.
- Artifacts: harness spec, sample prompts, and MAP timeline (attached).

Timeline (proposal):
- Jun 22: agree workload & SLOs (this thread)
- Jun 24–25: Redwood runs internal dry run and shares harness config
- Jun 29–Jul 2: joint benchmarking window (we schedule dedicated nodes)
- Jul 6: deliver results + recorded session
- Jul 9–12: evaluate results and surface acceptance decision
- Jul 15: target close (PO/contract signature)

Monica and Jordan — I've attached the harness spec and sample prompts; please flag anything missing. Emma — if that timeline looks tight, tell us where to relax.

Thanks,
Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Attachments: benchmark_harness_spec.pdf (12KB stub), sample_prompts.csv (3KB stub), MAP-timeline-v2.xlsx (5KB stub)
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Emma Dawson <emma@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 10:41:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME MAP: Benchmarking checklist, SLOs & close timeline

Thanks Rishi — quick notes from an ops/harness perspective. Attached is a pared-down harness spec with the exact payload shapes, measurement hooks (TTFT marker, token counters), and recommended warm-up sequence. Key clarifications:

- Workload mix: 60% short (<=64 tokens), 30% medium (65–256), 10% long (~512). We'll seed KV cache cases for the medium-path evaluations.
- Concurrency: we recommend running 3 concurrency tiers: 20, 50, 80 (ramp 10s -> steady 3m -> cool down).
- Measurement windows: 60s stability windows for throughput; TTFT measured on cold and warm prefixes separately.
- Cost estimate: dedicated run for 8 hours across 4 nodes (NVIDIA A100 equivalent) — estimate attached.

I'll schedule the dry run on our end for Jun 24 morning; Jordan — please confirm if dedicated capacity is OK to reserve for Jun 29.

- Monica

--
Monica Patel
Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Emma Dawson <emma@acme-corp.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME MAP: Benchmarking checklist, SLOs & close timeline

Confirmed — we can allocate the dedicated pool for Jun 29–Jul 2 as proposed. A couple of tweaks:

- Throughput target: let's provision to validate 50 reqs/sec sustained per instance (headroom) but keep acceptance at 40 reqs/sec. We'll document both in the MAP.
- Failover test: include cross-region fallback (us-east) for a 5% error injection scenario. That will validate our graceful degradation policy.
- Data handling: ACME asked for request-level auditing. We'll enable token-level tracing for the window and provide anonymized logs.

I've updated the MAP timeline in the shared Drive link. If ACME prefers a shorter close, we can compress evaluation and decision to Jul 6–8 but that requires immediate sign-off on workload today.

— Jordan

--
Jordan Blake
Director, Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
jordan_blake@redwood.com
From: Emma Dawson <emma@acme-corp.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, ACME DevOps <devops@acme-corp.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Jun 2026 11:20:00 -0400
Subject: Re: ACME MAP: Benchmarking checklist, SLOs & close timeline

Hi Rishi / Monica / Jordan,

Thanks for the clear plan and detailed harness. A few items from our side:

- Workload: agreed on the prompt mix. We'll provide 3 production prompt families plus 25 edge-case prompts (we'll upload these by EOD Jun 25).
- SLOs: the p95 < 650ms is acceptable; would you please add a p99 warning bracket (p99 < 900ms) so we can see tail behavior?
- TTFT: can you confirm how TTFT is measured (is it from request arrival to first token out)? We want the same definition in the MAP.
- Timeline: the Jun 29 window is okay but our legal needs to see the audit log handling note before the run. I've looped devops to ensure nothing blocks the dedicated pool.

If you can add p99 and the TTFT definition into the harness doc, we can keep your Jul 15 close target but request a soft acceptance review on Jul 9 instead of Jul 6.

Best,
Emma

Emma Dawson
Head of Platform Engineering, ACME Corporation
emma@acme-corp.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Emma Dawson <emma@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, ACME DevOps <devops@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2026 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME MAP: Benchmarking checklist, SLOs & close timeline

Emma — thanks for the quick clarifications and the prompt families you uploaded; we ran the joint window last week and have preliminary results. Summary and next steps: 

Summary (prelim):
- TTFT definition: measured as time from request arrival at front-end ingress to first token emitted. Harness includes cold-start and warm-start markers.
- Latency: median TTFT ~ 255ms; p95 observed 610ms; p99 observed 880ms in the burst tests.
- Throughput: sustained 46 reqs/sec per instance observed at the headroom run; acceptance threshold (40) met.
- Concurrency: stability at 80 concurrent simulated users had an error rate spike to 1.2% (target <1%). We'll run targeted remediation (tuning batching and KV priming) this week.
- Quality: automated evals show output-quality delta 1.3% relative to baseline; manual spot-checks look good.

Attachments: final run logs and the run-recording (links in Drive). Monica and Jordan will schedule a short remediation iteration and a follow-up verification run by Jul 14. If that run brings error rate under 1% and keeps p95 < 650ms, then we move the MAP to soft-acceptance review on Jul 15.

Next steps for ACME:
- Review run summary in Drive by Jul 13
- Confirm any compliance questions on audit logs (legal) so we keep the Jul 15 close

Thanks — will keep this thread updated as we close items.

Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
